summaries.information_need: A researcher comparing learning algorithms via hold out testing wants to know whether test error correlation arising from a shared training set undermines the standard variance estimator for prediction error, and whether ignoring this correlation biases confidence intervals used to judge significance of performance differences.

A researcher using K fold cross validation to compare algorithms wants to establish precisely which generalization error estimand the statistic targets, the error for one particular training set versus the error averaged over training set draws, and how the paired difference and jackknife estimators relate to this target under overlapping training folds.

A researcher wants to derive the error covariance structure among K fold cross validation test errors that arises from overlapping training sets and shared test blocks, and to determine how many distinct covariance components this permutation symmetry produces.

A researcher wants to establish under what conditions, if any, an unbiased variance estimator for K fold cross validation could exist across all data generating distributions, and how restricting attention to quadratic form estimators of the test errors and matching their expected moments against the true variance decomposition is used to derive the answer.
summaries.answer_type: existence proof via moment matching argument

summaries.information_need: A researcher wants to determine, via eigendecomposition of the cross validation error covariance matrix, why the variance component tied to the overall sample mean cannot be estimated from a single realization, and how the number of test blocks fixes the multiplicities of the remaining eigenvalues.

A researcher wants to know what constraints bound the within block and between block covariance parameters of K fold cross validation test errors relative to the marginal variance, and whether these bounds are tight enough to justify neglecting the parameters when building a variance estimate.

A researcher wants empirical evidence of how the magnitude of the three variance components of K fold cross validation shifts with training set size, outlier presence, and number of folds, in order to gauge how much bias a variance estimate that ignores error correlations could incur.
summaries.answer_type: empirical comparison across simulated and real data

summaries.information_need: A researcher wants to know how the special cases of K fold cross validation, hold out testing, two fold splitting, and leave one out sampling, affect whether an unbiased variance estimator becomes attainable, and under what structural condition on the between block covariance this happens.
summaries.primary_concept: special cases of K fold cross validation
sub_concepts: special cases of K fold cross validation
